name: Tile
author: frost
description: Fine specular over low metalness — floors and walls.

name: Emissive
author: frost
description: Material colour driven straight into emission — bulbs, neon and signage.

name: Wood
author: frost
description: Warm, rough surface with a light procedural grain and bump.

name: Brick
author: frost
description: High roughness and a weak highlight, for brickwork and masonry.

name: Plastic
author: frost
description: Clean, even non-metal with a controllable highlight.

name: Glass
author: frost
description: Clear, hard specular for panes and covers — as see-through as its material says head on, and a mirror at a grazing angle.

name: Concrete
author: frost
description: Fine-grained roughness with almost no gloss — walls and floors.

name: Stone
author: frost
description: Irregular mottled grain for stone walls, worktops and ornaments.

name: Fabric
author: frost
description: Dense weave and a soft highlight, for curtains and soft furnishing.

name: Rubber
author: frost
description: Matte and soft, for tyres, seals and soft plastics.

name: Leather
author: frost
description: Light grain and a gentle sheen, for sofas, bags and belts.

name: Paper
author: frost
description: Flat, matte and light — paper, posters and books.

name: Water
author: frost
description: Their own ripple map, tiled in world units and scrolled twice — after the Ripplet water of a Unity stage, whose reflection is the scene's own cubemap.

name: Gold
author: frost
description: Warm, fully metallic reflection for trim, frames and ornaments.

name: Mapped PBR
author: amyang-xyz
description: A surface that brought its own maps: the PMX texture for colour, a normal map in the first image slot and a packed property map (red metal, green roughness, blue occlusion) in the second.

name: Foliage
author: amyang-xyz
description: Leaves, grass and hedges — rough, unpolished, and no metal anywhere in it. Alpha-tested, so a leaf card keeps a crisp edge and occludes the canopy behind it.

name: Stage Surface
author: frost
description: Metal, roughness and occlusion taken from the material itself — what a converted stage packs into its PMX specular. One look for a whole set, varying per material.
